sights.name: Acropolis and Parthenon
sights.summary: The rock of Athens, crowned by the Parthenon, the most famous temple in the world.

sights.name: Areopagus (Mars Hill)
sights.summary: The rocky hill where the Apostle Paul preached to the Athenians.

sights.name: Acropolis Museum
sights.summary: A glass museum over ancient ruins, holding the treasures of the Acropolis.

sights.name: Ancient Agora
sights.summary: The marketplace and civic heart of ancient Athens, with its best-preserved temple.

sights.name: Plaka and Anafiotika
sights.summary: The old neighborhood under the Acropolis, with a Cycladic village hidden on its slope.

sights.name: Syntagma Square and the changing of the guard
parts: The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
sights.summary: The Parliament and the Evzones guards in pleated kilts and pom-pom shoes.

sights.name: Athens Cathedral and the Little Metropolis
sights.summary: The seat of the Greek Orthodox Church, beside a tiny 12th-century chapel.

sights.name: Monastiraki and the flea market
sights.summary: A buzzing square with a mosque, a church and lanes of shops.

sights.name: Temple of Olympian Zeus and Hadrian's Arch
parts: The temple that took six centuries
sights.summary: Giant columns of the largest temple in ancient Greece.

sights.name: Lycabettus Hill
sights.summary: The highest point in the city, with a chapel on top and views to the sea.

sights.name: Theatre of Dionysus
sights.summary: The birthplace of Western theater, on the south slope of the Acropolis.

sights.name: Acropolis promenade (Dionysiou Areopagitou and Apostolou Pavlou)
sights.summary: The car-free walk that circles below the Acropolis, past cafés, olive trees and views.

sights.name: Agia Ekaterini (St Catherine's Church)
sights.summary: A small 11th-century Byzantine church in Plaka, sunk below street level among Roman columns.

sights.name: Panagia Kapnikarea
sights.summary: An 11th-century Byzantine church standing in the middle of Ermou, Athens' busiest shopping street.

sights.name: Roman Agora and Tower of the Winds
sights.summary: The Roman-era marketplace, with an ancient weather station and water clock.

sights.name: National Archaeological Museum
sights.summary: Greece's greatest museum of ancient art, from gold masks to the world's oldest computer.

sights.name: Byzantine and Christian Museum
sights.summary: Icons, mosaics and frescoes telling the story of Christianity in Greece.

sights.name: National Garden
sights.summary: A shady royal garden behind Parliament, with ponds, ruins and quiet paths.

sights.name: Philopappos Hill
sights.summary: The pine-covered hill facing the Acropolis, with the city's best sunset view.

sights.name: Ancient Corinth
sights.travel: About 1 hour 15 minutes each way by car or tour; stop at the Corinth Canal on the way.
sights.summary: The city where Paul lived for 18 months and wrote to the Corinthians.

sights.name: Temple of Poseidon at Sounion
sights.travel: About 1 hour 15 minutes each way along the coast road.
sights.summary: A marble temple on a cliff at the tip of Attica, famous at sunset.

sights.name: Delphi
sights.travel: About 2 hours 30 minutes each way by car or tour: a full day.
sights.summary: The sanctuary of the oracle, on a mountainside above an olive valley.

sights.name: Corinth Canal
sights.travel: About 1 hour west of Athens by car or tour coach on the highway; trains run to Corinth, then a short taxi.
sights.summary: A narrow, dizzying cut through solid rock linking the Aegean and Ionian seas.

sights.name: Acrocorinth
sights.travel: A 10-minute drive up from Ancient Corinth (about 1 hour 20 minutes from Athens); taxis wait at Ancient Corinth.
sights.summary: The mighty fortress on the mountain above Ancient Corinth.
